evidence.text: 漢典 records the Shuowen account as “助也。从口从又” and an alternative text “手口相助也。从又从口.” Its quoted Duan Yucai commentary explains it as hand supplemented by mouth, while another note disputes that analysis and questions the received component order. The entry also records right-hand and right-side senses, along with older cited uses of 右 for helping, blessing, and urging food. These are dictionary records of textual citations, not independent dates for the character's graphic formation.
evidence.title: 右 yòu - 汉典

evidence.source: Kotobank, 普及版 字通 entry for 右
evidence.field: 字形 / 訓義 / 聲系
evidence.text: The 字通 account analyzes 又 as a right hand and 口 as a ritual prayer vessel, and connects the graph with ritual service and later assistance. It explicitly rejects the Shuowen/Duan hand-and-mouth explanation as the graph's actual formation. It says oracle-bone 右/又 forms were used for divine assistance and notes assistance examples in bronze inscriptions. This is an alternative scholarly interpretation; the page does not establish that 口 was merely a meaningless distinguishing mark.
evidence.title: 右(ウ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.text: The page catalogs an oracle-bone example as 鐵7.4 合20836 and bronze forms including 右作旅鼎 and several early Western Zhou inscriptions, and lists Chu manuscripts, Shuowen seal script, Qin slips, and clerical forms. The catalog indicates graphic attestations across those script collections, but the page supplies no date for the oracle-bone example and I did not inspect its glyph images; it therefore does not establish a precise first occurrence or the proposed graphic transition sequence.

evidence.text: Search-indexed text of Shuowen gives “右：手口相助也.” The associated Shuowen tradition is a historical explanation, not direct confirmation of the graph's original construction. The page search result was found, but opening it returned HTTP 403, so the entry itself could not be inspected directly.
evidence.title: 右 - 中國哲學書電子化計劃

evidence.text: The dictionary separately lists 右 for helping (with citations to Shuowen, Yi, Zhouli, Zuozhuan, and Shijing), blessing/protecting (Shijing and Hanshu examples), right hand, right side, west, high status, and urging food (interpreted as 侑). This supports that the graph was used for more than the directional meaning, but the cited classical works do not by themselves establish which sense was earliest. The links among assistance, divine blessing, ritual service, and direction remain interpretive rather than a demonstrated chronological chain.

evidence.text: The entry reports 又 as Mandarin yòu and Baxter–Sagart 2011 Old Chinese *ɢʷəʔ-s (with variant notation *[ɢ]ʷəʔ-s), and Middle Chinese hjuwH. This is a secondary transcription, not an opened primary table; no local 又 row was supplied for Baxter–Sagart cross-checking. Similar reconstructed shapes support a possible sound relationship only tentatively here and do not independently establish the component's phonetic role or the history of a whole-graph loan.
evidence.title: 又 - 维基词典，自由的多语言词典

evidence.text: The entry reports 右 as Mandarin yòu, Middle Chinese hjuwX, Baxter–Sagart *[ɢ]ʷəʔ, and Zhengzhang *ɢʷɯʔ. Its displayed Baxter–Sagart form matches the supplied local Baxter–Sagart row's first reading; the local row also includes a distinct departing-tone reading, hjuwH, *[ɢ]ʷəʔ-s (~ *m-qʷəʔ). The candidate phonetic 又 is therefore not simply identical to every reading associated with 右; this alone neither proves nor disproves a phonetic role, and the dataset notation must remain system-specific.
evidence.title: 右 - 维基词典，自由的多语言词典

evidence.text: The entry gives the two Guangyun-style readings: 于救切, departing tone, and 云久切, rising tone, as well as the modern Mandarin reading yòu. These are separate reading records; the site's traditional and dictionary-based notation should not be merged with Baxter–Sagart reconstructions.
